good_evening.note: For daylight hours into dusk; after dark, Malaysians switch to selamat malam.

goodbye.note: 'See you again'; selamat tinggal is a more final, formal farewell.

how_are_you.note: The kh is a soft, breathy sound, like clearing your throat gently.

slang.note: Literally 'what's the story'; casual, for friends and peers only.

no_problem.note: The reply to thanks; 'no worries' is tak apa.

please.note: Tolong asks for help; sila is used on signs and formal invitations.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'may I ask'; use to get someone's attention politely.

no.note: In casual speech Malaysians shorten this to tak.

slang.note: Borrowed straight from English; casual and safe with anyone friendly.
Playful and expressive; great with friends or the food vendor.

cheers.note: Literally 'drink'; a simple, sober-friendly invitation to toast.

slang.note: The classic shout at Malaysian dinners and weddings; drag out 'yam' then snap 'seng' with the group.
